outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector (1–5 days, $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts) and file a Fictitious Business Name statement if the DBA differs from the legal entity name. What to say: Apply for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate online or in person, providing the EIN and entity name. The registration year runs April 1 to March 31; pro-rate the fee if opening mid-year. Every other city department asks for the Business Account Number (BAN), so complete this immediately. File the FBN statement with the County Clerk, publish in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks, and file proof of publication within 45 days.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain a certified food protection manager certificate (ANSI-accredited exam, $100–$250, 1–14 days) for the owner or a manager, required before the DPH pre-opening inspection. What to say: Enroll in an ANSI-accredited food safety certification course (ServSafe, Prometric, NRFSP or 360training), pass the proctored exam, and receive the certificate (valid 5 years). At least one owner or employee must hold a current certificate before the mobile food facility health permit is issued. All other food-handling employees must obtain California food handler cards within 30 days of hire.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the mobile food facility health permit application to SF Department of Public Health (30–90 days, $880–$1,500 including plan review and inspection). What to say: Submit two sets of scaled drawings of the food truck (interior layout, equipment, finishes, water/wastewater systems), exterior and interior photos, the menu, a commissary agreement with a licensed facility, the certified food manager certificate, and the BAN through the DPH portal. Schedule the vehicle inspection after plan approval. DPH will send the application to Planning for a zoning referral; if a CUA is pending, inform DPH and request that the referral wait until the CUA is approved to avoid a zoning objection that blocks the health permit.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If the truck will occupy public right-of-way, file the Public Works mobile food facility location permit application after the health permit is issued (60–180 days, $1,151+ starting fee, with 30-day public comment period and potential hearing). What to say: Identify 2–3 candidate street locations within the C-2/Waterfront 2 area and file a location permit application for each with SF Public Works Bureau of Street-Use & Mapping, paying half of the processing, notification and inspection fees up front. Post a notice at each site for 10 days and mail notification to everyone within 75 feet. The 30-day comment period follows; unresolved objections trigger a public hearing. Final issuance requires the DPH mobile health permit, SFFD certificate, DMV registration and $2M liability insurance naming the City. Expect neighbor appeals from nearby restaurants; apply for multiple locations and be prepared to negotiate hours, location and operational details to resolve objections. If the outdoor seating area is entirely on private property, confirm with Planning and Public Works in writing that no location permit is needed.
